text:
Droit de la famille — 241452

2024 QCCS 3547

SUPERIOR COURT

CANADA

PROVINCE OF QUÉBEC

DISTRICT OF

MONTRÉAL

(Civil Division)

No :

500-12-354352-225

DATE :

September 23, 2024

______________________________________________________________________

BEFORE THE HONOURABLE

ENRICO
FORLINI, J.C.S.

______________________________________________________________________

A. H.

Plaintiff

v.

S. T.

Defendant

______________________________________________________________________

JUDGMENT

(Application for Revocation -
art. 345-346
C.p.c.
)

______________________________________________________________________

OVERVIEW

[
1
]

On March 13, 24, 2024, the Superior Court rendered a divorce
judgment (“
Judgment of Divorce
”) and granted a divorce between the
parties.

[
2
]

The Defendant asks the Court to revoke the Judgment of Divorce.

[
3
]

In her Application for Revocation
[1]
,
she principally alleges her religious belief that prohibit divorce as a reason
justifying the revocation. The Defendant also alleges other reasons including
(i) the Judgment is unfair, (ii) she did not attend the trial because of a
physical illness, and (iii) the interests of justice.
[2]

[
4
]

The Plaintiff argues that the Application for Revocation should be
dismissed because it was served beyond the thirty-day delay of article 347 of
the
Code of Civil Procedure
(“
C.C.P.
”), and moreover,
because the reasons justifying the revocation are baseless and not supported by
the evidence.

[
5
]

This judgment
adjudicates the Application
for Revocation at the second stage, in other words, the merits of the reasons
for revocation
.

[
6
]

For the reasons expressed below, the Application for Revocation is
dismissed because it is time-barred and since the reasons justifying the
revocation are without merit and constitute a pretext for the Defendant’s
negligence.

CONTEXT

[
7
]

The Application for Revocation arises in the following context, as
it was aptly summarized by Justice Dubé in her judgment rendered on May 3, 2024,
dismissing the Plaintiff’s application to dismiss (art. 168
C.C.P.
) the Defendant’s
Application for Revocation:

CONTEXT

[4]

The parties were married on January 18,
1998, under the matrimonial regime of partnership of acquests. They have a
daughter born in 2000. They lived under the same roof until the end of 2021,
but the husband considers that the relationship was terminated in 2017.

[5]

They are co-owners of a duplex in Town A,
one floor of which was the family residence. Plaintiff owns five other
properties: two in Sweden, one in town B, one in Town C and one in Town D. He
declared having a net value of $3,103,362.62 $ on June 28, 2023.

[6]

On July 18, 2022, the Plaintiff served and
filed an Application to Institute Proceedings and divorce.

[7]

On July 25, 2022, the Defendant filed an
Answer, through her former lawyers, Me Geneviève Grey and Me Julius Grey.

[8]

On October 26, 2022, the parties signed a
Case Protocol.

[9]

On or about April 20, 2023, the Defendant
signed a Defence and a Cross-demand with an application for the issuance of
safeguard and provisional orders, which was presentable on June 20, 2023.

[10]

On June 16, 2023, in anticipation to the June 20, 2023 hearing, the
Plaintiff filed a sworn statement undertaking not to sell any immoveable or
moveable property included in the family patrimony or the partnership of
acquests without Defendant’s or the Court’s authorization, until the final
divorce judgment.

[11]

On June 28, 2023, the Plaintiff filed a Form III, his Statement of
the family patrimony and of the partnership of acquests.

[12]

On July 17, 2023, Defendant’s attorneys served a Notice of intent to
cease representing.

[13]

On July 18, 2023, the Plaintiff filed his
Demande
d’inscription pour instruction et jugement
.

[14]

On July 19, 2023, a Notice to appoint a new attorney or to indicate
intention to self-represent was served by bailiffs on Defendant personally.

[15]

On September 13, 2023, a notice of incomplete file was emailed to
the parties, by the
Direction des rôles civils et jugements
.

[16]

On September 25, 2023, the Plaintiff filed his missing exhibits and
Declaration under Article 444
C.C.P.

[17]

Defendant never filed her Statements of family patrimony and of the
partnership of acquests.

[18]

On November 23, 2023, Plaintiff’s Notice of case management asking
to schedule a trial date by default was served by bailiffs and received by the
parties’ daughter, at the Defendant’s residence.

[19]

On December 6, 2023, the Defendant did not appear in Court and the
Notice of case management was granted. The hearing by default of the divorce on
the merits was scheduled for March 12, 2024. The Court also authorized the
notification of any proceedings and exhibits to Defendant by technological
means at her email address.

[20]

On February 6, 2024, the Plaintiff modified his divorce application
and served Defendant by email.

[21]

On March 12, 2024, the hearing proceeded by default.

[22]

On March 13, 2024 a divorce judgment was rendered granting
Plaintiff’s modified divorce application. This judgment:

•
Orders the sale of the family residence and the eviction of
Defendant by July 1,
,
2024;

•
Grants Plaintiff $70,000 as a rental indemnity to be
subtracted from her share of the family residence;

•
Orders the partition of the value of the family patrimony and
of the partnership of acquests as of July 1, 2017, which results in the payment
of $530,571.61  and an RRSP rollover of $100,232.88 to Defendant.

[
8
]

To this summary, the Court adds the following.

[
9
]

On May 23, following Justice Dubé’s judgment, the parties’ filed a
Joint Declaration for the Purpose of Scheduling a Hearing.

[
10
]

The Application for Revocation was heard on
September 18, 2024. The parties were informed prior to this hearing that the
hearing would address the “second stage” of an application for revocation, in
other words, the merits of the reasons for revocation
[3]
.

ANALYSIS

1.

THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK

[
11
]

The procedure to revoke a judgment is
exceptional. This principle was reiterated by the Court of Appeal in
Fabrikant

v
. Concordia University
as follows
[4]
:

3. Motions for revocation are an
exception to the well established and important rules protecting the finality
and the stability of civil judgments. They are not meant to relitigate issues
already decided by a court, because a litigant disagrees with the judgment. A judgment
is not null because a party thinks it rests on an inaccurate statement of the
law or a misinterpretation of the facts.

[
12
]

The rules governing the revocation of a judgment
are set out in articles 345 to 348 of the
Code of Civil Procedure
.

[
13
]

Pursuant to article 347
C.C.P.
, the
application for revocation must be served within strict time limits, namely
within 30 days after the party became aware of the judgment.

[
14
]

As for the reasons which justify the revocation
of a judgment, they are set forth in articles 345 and 346
C.C.P.
:

345.
Le jugement peut, à la demande d’une partie, être rétracté
par le tribunal qui l’a rendu si son maintien est susceptible de déconsidérer
l’administration de la justice; il en est ainsi si le jugement a été rendu
par suite du dol d’une autre partie ou sur des pièces fausses ou si la
production de pièces décisives avait été empêchée par force majeure ou par le
fait d’une autre partie.

Le jugement peut aussi être
rétracté dans les cas suivants:

1°  le jugement a
prononcé au-delà des conclusions ou a omis de statuer sur une des conclusions
de la demande;

2°  aucune défense
valable n’a été produite au soutien des droits d’un mineur ou d’un majeur en
tutelle ou d’une personne dont le mandat de protection a été homologué;

3°  il a été statué sur
la foi d’un consentement invalide ou à la suite d’offres non autorisées et
ultérieurement désavouées;

4°  il a été découvert
après le jugement une preuve qui aurait probablement entraîné un jugement
différent, si elle avait pu être connue en temps utile par la partie
concernée ou par son avocat alors même que ceux-ci ont agi avec toute la
diligence raisonnable.

346
. La partie condamnée par défaut, faute de répondre à
l’assignation, de participer à la conférence de gestion ou de contester au
fond, peut, si elle a été empêchée de se défendre par fraude, par surprise ou
par une autre cause jugée suffisante, s’adresser au tribunal qui a rendu le
jugement pour demander que celui-ci soit rétracté et la demande originaire rejetée.

Le pourvoi en rétractation
contient non seulement les motifs qui justifient la rétractation, mais aussi
les moyens de défense à la demande originaire.

345
. A judgment may, on a party’s application, be revoked by the
court that rendered it
if letting the judgment stand would tend to bring
the administration of justice into disrepute
. The judgment may be
revoked, for instance, if fraud was committed by another party, if the
judgment was based on false exhibits or if the production of decisive
exhibits was prevented by superior force or by the act or omission of another
party.

As well, a judgment may be
revoked if

(1)  the judgment adjudicated
beyond the conclusions set out in the application or did not rule on one of
them;

(2)  no valid defence was produced
in support of the rights of a minor or of a person of full age under
tutorship or for whom a protection mandate has been homologated;

(3)  a ruling was made on the
basis of invalid consent or following an unauthorized tender that was
subsequently disavowed; or

(4)  evidence was subsequently
discovered that would probably have led to a different judgment if the party
concerned or its lawyer had become aware of that evidence in sufficient time,
although they acted with due diligence.

346.
A party against which a
default judgment
has been rendered
following failure to answer the summons, attend the case management
conference or defend on the merits but that
was prevented from doing so
owing to fraud, surprise or any other cause considered sufficient
may apply
to the court that rendered the judgment for the revocation of the judgment
and the dismissal of the original application.

The application for revocation
must contain the reasons justifying the revocation as well as the grounds of
defence raised against the original application.

[
15
]

A judgment may be revoked under article 345
C.C.P.

if the applicant proves that “letting the judgment stand would tend to bring
the administration of justice into disrepute”.  Examples of such a
situation are set out in paragraphs 1 and 2 of the article. These reasons are
not exhaustive. However, a ground for revocation not listed in paragraphs 1 to
4 of the second paragraph of article 345
C.C.P.
must, at the very least,
tend to bring the administration of justice into disrepute
[5]
.

[
16
]

In
Allianz Global Risks US Insurance Company
v.

SNC-Lavalin inc.
, the Court of Appeal writes that when a party relies on
article 345
C.C.P.
, the reason it invokes to revocate the judgment must
be sufficiently serious so as to conclude that the very basis of the judgment
is seriously and irreparably flailed
[6]
:

[
17
]

The authors Ferland & Emery summarize as
follows what this concept entails:
[7]

Motif général de déconsidération de l'administration de la justice

2-81 –
Le jugement peut, à la demande d'une partie, être rétracté par le tribunal qui
l'a rendu si son maintien est susceptible de déconsidérer l'administration de
la justice ; il en est ainsi si le jugement a été rendu par suite du
dol d'une autre partie ou sur des pièces fausses ou si la production de
pièces décisives avait été empêchée par force majeure, mais non par le simple
manque de diligence de la partie, ou par le fait d'une autre partie ou si
le tribunal a été privé d'informations pertinentes et essentielles (art. 345,
al. 1).

2-82 –
Le terme « dol » comprend la notion d'un artifice en vue d'induire en erreur la
partie avec qui un contrat est conclu. Un jugement qui a « donné acte » d'une
convention de partage du patrimoine familial ne constitue pas un obstacle
infranchissable à son annulation s'il y a eu de fausses allégations et des
manoeuvres dolosives à l'endroit d'une partie ; une telle demande d'annulation
doit respecter les conditions de fond prévues au
Code de procédure
civile
en matière de rétractation de jugement.

2-83 –
L'insatisfaction des services rendus par l'avocat et du jugement rendu n'est
pas un motif de rétractation visé par cette disposition (art. 345).

2-84 –
Ainsi, au-delà des motifs énumérés par le Code, le législateur introduit un
critère plus général tiré d'une jurisprudence qui a considéré cette énumération
comme n'étant pas limitative, soit le critère de la déconsidération de
l'administration de la justice, critère déjà retenu au
Code civil du
Québec
comme motif de rejet d'un élément de preuve (
art.
2858
C.c.Q.).

2-85 –
Cette jurisprudence s'inspirait notamment d'un arrêt de la Cour d'appel selon
lequel « une demande en rétractation doit être accueillie chaque fois qu'il
s'agit de remédier à une injustice grave ne provenant pas de la faute grossière
de la partie lésée ».

2-86 –
Selon la Cour d'appel, la notion de déconsidération de la justice « fait appel
à la subjectivité et relève d'une certaine appréciation judiciaire ». L'état
d'esprit du juge, tant en matière civile qu'en matière pénale, se doit d'être
le même lorsqu'il doit statuer sur la notion de « déconsidération de
l'administration de la justice ». Le pouvoir discrétionnaire est enraciné dans
les valeurs de la société et, en particulier, ses valeurs à long terme. Il ne
doit pas rendre une décision que la société considérerait comme inacceptable
lorsque celle-ci n'est pas déchirée par la passion ou autrement tiraillée par
des événements présents.

2-87 –
Enfin, selon la Cour d'appel, avant l'introduction au nouveau Code du motif
général de la déconsidération de l'administration de la justice (art.
345
, al. 1), le non-respect du devoir d'impartialité du juge au
cours du déroulement du procès n'était pas un motif de rétractation du
jugement.

[
Citations
omitted]

[
18
]

In
Lepointdevente.com
v.
Festival
de jazz de Québec
, Justice Christian Brunelle, j.q.c. made a detailed
analysis of what situations could be considered to bring the administration of
justice into disrepute
[8]
:

[48]
Au premier alinéa de l’article 345 C.p.c., le
législateur semble d’ailleurs accorder une très grande importance à la
recherche de la vérité. Il y énonce deux situations où le tribunal paraît
justifié de conclure que le maintien d’un jugement « est susceptible de
déconsidérer l’administration de la justice » :

-
Première situation : « …le jugement a été rendu par
suite du dol d’une autre partie ou sur des pièces fausses… »;

-
Deuxième situation : « …la production de pièces
décisives avait été empêchée par force majeure ou par le fait d’une autre
partie ».

[49]
Ainsi, la partie qui obtient un jugement en sa faveur
par suite de manœuvres trompeuses ou malhonnêtes, de fausses représentations,
de réticences ou de silences, ou par suite de la falsification de documents ou
de la dissimulation de pièces décisives, par mauvaise foi ou négligence, ne
devrait pas pouvoir tirer profit de son mépris pour la vérité et de sa propre
turpitude.

[50]
Les deux situations expressément ciblées par le
législateur ne sont évidemment pas les seules que peut recouper « le motif
général de la déconsidération de la justice ». L’expression
« for instance », que l’on trouve dans la version anglaise du texte
de l’article 345 C.p.c., indique bien que ces situations sont des exemples
non limitatifs.

[51]
À titre d’exemples additionnels, le juge qui manque à son devoir
d’impartialité ou bafoue le droit d’une partie à une défense pleine et
entière peut lui-même déconsidérer, par son comportement, l’administration
de la justice.

[52]
Le tribunal appelé à appliquer l’article 345 C.p.c.
doit donc déterminer si, « aux yeux d’une personne raisonnable, objective
et bien informée de toutes les circonstances de l’affaire »,
l’administration de la justice serait déconsidérée si le jugement, objet du
pourvoi en rétractation, est maintenu.

[53]
Par exemple, le pourvoi devrait être accueilli quand
la partie contre laquelle il est formé a tenté de cacher « un acte
potentiellement fautif […] et d'empêcher, en masquant la vérité, le
fonctionnement du système de justice ».

[54]
C’est à ce prix que l’on peut maintenir l’autorité des
tribunaux et « la confiance du public dans le système de justice
civile » :

L’expression « déconsidérer
l’administration de la justice » doit être prise dans l’optique du
maintien à long terme de l’intégrité du système de justice et de la confiance à
son égard.

[
Citations
omitted]

[
19
]

Article 346
C.C.P.
addresses applications
for revocation when the judgment has been granted by default. In such a case,
the judgment may be revoked if the moving party proves that it was prevented
from answering the summons, attending the case management conference or defending
on the merits “owing to fraud, surprise or any other cause considered sufficient.”

[
20
]

The courts have decided applications for revocation
raising this reason on numerous occasions.

[
21
]

One constant rule stands out: the absence of
follow-up, the carelessness, negligence, incompetence, or laxity of a litigant
cannot serve as a basis for the revocation of a judgment under article 346
C.C.P.

[
22
]

Revocation of judgments for valid reasons of fraud,
surprise or any other cause deemed sufficient, are numerous and necessary, as
these do not endanger the principle of the stability of judgments. This
principle must yield to the fundamental principle of the right to be heard.
This requires correcting errors if it can be done without causing prejudice to
the opposing party.

[
23
]

According to the Court of Appeal in
Groupe
JSV Inc.
v.
Goal Capital Inc
., even a stupid mistake can justify the
revocation of a judgment when the party also has serious grounds of defense, as
long as the behavior of the party does not demonstrate that the application for
revocation is a dilatory maneuver or that he has shown a disregard towards the
judicial system.

[
24
]

Authors Benoit Emery and Denis Ferland express
the following regarding situations that may lead to the revocation of a
judgment under article 346
C.C.P.
:

2-93
–
D'autre part, l'erreur d'un avocat qui notamment a omis de comparaître
(ancienne comparution avant le nouveau Code) ou de plaider dans le délai, sans
demander la prorogation consensuelle ou judiciaire de ce délai, avant jugement
rendu par défaut contre son client défendeur
, ou une
irrégularité de signification de l'acte introductif d'instance
,
ou l'impossibilité du défendeur d'agir ou de communiquer dans le délai légal,
en raison de son état ou de son éloignement, à l'époque de l'instance, peuvent
constituer, selon les circonstances laissées à l'appréciation du tribunal, une
« autre cause jugée suffisante » de rétractation de jugement.

2-94
–
Le comportement négligent de la partie elle-même ne peut constituer une cause
suffisante de rétractation de jugement
.
[9]

[Citations omitted]

[
25
]

For his part, the author François-Olivier
Barbeau summarizes the situations where judgments have been revoked under this
article:

23.  Comportement
diligent.

– Outre les cas relevant de la
surprise ou de la fraude, l’article 346
C.p.c.
(2014)
autorise la rétractation lorsque la partie condamnée démontre qu’elle a été
empêchée de se défendre par une « autre cause jugée suffisante ».
L’analyse de la jurisprudence révèle que les circonstances susceptibles de
constituer une « autre cause jugée suffisante » sont variées et que
chaque cas doit être évalué selon l’ensemble des circonstances propres au
dossier.

L’analyse de la suffisance des
motifs de rétractation invoqués relève, en premier lieu, de l’appréciation du
comportement de la partie condamnée par défaut. Il incombe à cette dernière de
démontrer que son défaut résulte non pas de sa propre négligence, mais d’une
impossibilité d’agir, d’une erreur de fait excusable ou de circonstances
extérieures, tels le fait de la partie adverse ou d’un tiers dont elle ne répond
pas. Cette appréciation doit tenir compte de l’ensemble des circonstances du
dossier
et du sérieux des moyens de défenses
invoqués à l’encontre de la demande originaire.

À l’opposé, les tribunaux
manifestent peu d’indulgence à l’égard d’une partie qui fait preuve d’un manque
de sérieux dans la conduite de ses affaires en omettant d’assurer un suivi
adéquat de son dossier. Ils ont maintes fois réitéré que la négligence d’une
partie ou de l’un de ses préposés ne constitue pas une cause suffisante
de rétractation. Une partie ne peut faire preuve d’insouciance, de laxisme ou
d’un manque de sérieux dans la conduite d’une affaire judiciaire qui la
concerne et doit plutôt agir promptement et de manière diligente afin d’assurer
la sauvegarde de ses droits. Il a également été décidé que le manque
d’organisation interne au sein d’une compagnie ou la simple ignorance des
conséquences de son défaut ne constitue pas un motif valable de rétractation.
Ce refus de reconnaître que la négligence puisse servir de fondement à une
demande de rétractation de jugement a été justifié par le principe de
l’irrévocabilité des jugements et par le souci de préserver la stabilité des
rapports juridiques.

24.  Causes jugées
suffisantes

– De manière générale, les
tribunaux reconnaissent que la cause de rétractation jugée suffisante peut
résulter d’une méprise, d’un imbroglio ou d’une erreur « excusable »
causée par des circonstances extérieures à la partie elle-même, par le fait de
la partie adverse ou par un tiers. Le tribunal doit alors déterminer si la
méprise ou l’erreur invoquée pour justifier le défaut résulte du laxisme de la
partie condamnée, auquel cas la rétractation sera refusée. À l’inverse, le
jugement sera susceptible d’être rétracté lorsque l’erreur « excusable »
est la cause véritable de l’inaction de la partie condamnée par défaut. Les tribunaux examineront également l’attitude de la partie
condamnée dans la conduite de ses affaires et le suivi de ses dossiers.
[10]

[References omitted]

[
26
]

Furthermore, when, as in this case, a party
alleges that their physical, psychological, or other health issue has prevented
it from understanding the nature of the proceedings and the importance of
responding to them or attending the trial, in other words, that they were faced
with an impossibility or incapacity to act and therefore have a sufficient reason
for revoking a judgment, the Court of Appeal teaches that as a general rule,
expert testimony must be adduced to prove an allegation of this nature.
[11]

2.

APPLICATION TO THE FACTS OF THIS CASE

2.1

Is the Application for Revocation Time-Barred?

[
27
]

The Plaintiff argues that the Defendant became
aware of the Judgment of Divorce on March 13, 2024, but served her Application
for Revocation on April 22, 2024, beyond the thirty-day limit prescribed in
article 347
C.C.P.

347.
Le pourvoi en rétractation est signifié à toutes les parties
à l’instance
dans les 30 jours qui suivent
le jour où est disparue la
cause qui empêchait la partie de produire sa défense ou celui où
la partie
a acquis connaissance du jugement
, de la preuve ou du fait donnant
ouverture à la rétractation. S’agissant d’un mineur, ce délai court depuis la
notification du jugement faite depuis qu’il a atteint sa majorité.

Le pourvoi en rétractation est
présenté au tribunal dans les 30 jours qui suivent la signification, comme
s’il s’agissait d’une demande en cours d’instance. Il ne peut l’être s’il
s’est écoulé plus de six mois depuis le jugement.

Ces délais sont de rigueur.

347.
An application for revocation must be served on all parties
to the proceeding
within 30 days
after the day on which the cause
preventing the party from filing a defence ceased to exist, or
after the
day on which the party became aware of the judgment
, evidence or fact
that constitutes grounds for the revocation. In the case of a minor, the
30-day period only begins to run as of notification of the judgment after the
person reaches full age.

The application for revocation
must be presented before the court within 30 days after service, as if it
were an application in the course of a proceeding. It cannot be presented if
more than six months have elapsed since the judgment.

These are strict time limits.

[Underlining added]

[
28
]

There is no dispute as to the fact that the
Application for Revocation was served on April 22, 2024
[12]
.

[
29
]

The issue is on what date did she become aware
of the Judgment of Divorce?

[
30
]

The trial took place on March 12, 2024.

[
31
]

The Judgment of Divorce was issued on March 13,
2024.

[
32
]

On the same day, at 12:33 PM, the trial judge’s
assistant sent a copy of the Judgment of Divorce to the parties or their
lawyers by email.
[13]

[
33
]

The email was addressed to the Defendant at an
email address which she confirms is her email address and which she had access
to on a regular and on-going basis. The record shows that she used this email
address to communicate with court staff prior to the trial and after it. There
is no question that she was able to send and receive communications and
documents by email.
[14]

[
34
]

It is true that in her Application for
Revocation, the Defendant alleges that she learned about the Judgment of
Divorce on March 26, 2024, when it was served on her by a bailiff.
[15]

[
35
]

Indeed, the record shows that on that date, a
bailiff attended to her residence to try to serve the Judgment of Divorce on
her. Upon ringing the door, no one answered. The bailiff’s report states that
the bailiff waited in his car and when he noticed that a woman was about to
enter the premises through the front door, he walked up to her, identified
himself as a bailiff, and asked her if she was indeed the Defendant. She denied
being the Defendant. He reitered his request and only then did she confirm that
she was indeed the Defendant. At this point, he remitted the judgment to her
personally.
[16]

[
36
]

The fact that the Defendant denied being who she
was when first asked by the bailiff shows that she attempted to avoid service
of legal pleadings.

[
37
]

However, the evidence shows that she also received
the Judgment of Divorce when it was sent to her by email by the trial judge’s
assistant on March 13, 2024. She acknowledges that she received the email and
that “for sure, they sent it [the judgment] on that day [March 13, 2024]”.

[
38
]

The Defendant acknowledges that she receives “a
lot of emails, and all I do, I just delete all the emails that I receive”.
[17]

[
39
]

The preponderance of the evidence establishes
that the Defendant became aware of the Judgment of Divorce on March 13, 2024, yet
served her Application for Revocation on April 22, 2024, which is beyond the
strict time limit provided for in article 347
C.C.P.
to serve the
Application for Revocation.

[
40
]

For this reason alone, her Application for
Revocation of the Judgment of Divorce must be dismissed.
[18]

2.2

Was the Defendant Prevented from Attending the Trial because of Fraud,
Surprise or Any Other Cause Considered Sufficient?

[
41
]

At the September 18 hearing on the Application
for Revocation, she did not testify as to her reported inability to attend the
trial because of a physical illness. However, since the Defendant alleges in
her Modified Application for Revocation dated May 16, 2024, that at some point
in time, she was on sick leave, the Court will address this reason.
[19]

[
42
]

The Plaintiff’s Application for Divorce was
filed and served in July 2022.

[
43
]

On July 25, 2022, the Defendant filed an answer
and indicated that she would be represented by the law firm Grey Casgrain.

[
44
]

The Defendant was represented by this law firm
until July 17, 2023. On that day, her lawyers filed a Notice of Intent to Cease
Representing.

[
45
]

On July 17, 2023, Plaintiff’s lawyers filed a
request to have the case set down for trial and judgment since the delay to do
so expired on July 18, 2023.

[
46
]

On July 19, 2023, the Plaintiff served the
Defendant with a Notice to Appoint a New Attorney or to indicate her intention
to self represent.

[
47
]

On Novembre 22, 2023, the Plaintiff filed a
Notice for Case Management in which he notably alleged that he had been without
any news from the Defendant since July 19, 2023, and that she was not
collaborating to have the file set down for trial. He asked the Court to
schedule the trial on the merits.

[
48
]

This Notice of Case Management was heard by the
Court on December 6, 2023. The Defendant did not attend the hearing despite
being duly served with the Notice of Case Management.

[
49
]

On December 6, the Court scheduled the trial of
the merits on the Divorce Application for March 12, 2024.

[
50
]

The Court also ordered the Defendant to
communicate to the Plaintiff’s attorney by no later than January 31, 2024, her
Form III, her Declaration under article 444
C.C.P.
and her Statement of Family
Patrimony and Partnership of Acquests.

[
51
]

The Defendant never communicated these documents
to the Plaintiff’s attorneys.

[
52
]

The Defendant was served with the minutes of the
December 6, 2023 judgment, both by the Court staff and by Plaintiff’s lawyers.
[20]

[
53
]

The Defendant knew at the latest on February 6,
2024 that the trial on the merits of the Application for Divorce was to take
place beginning on March 12 at the Montreal Courthouse.

[
54
]

On February 27, 2024, she was again informed by
the Judge responsible for the Family Practice Court (room 2.01) during the week
of March 11, 2024, that the trial would take place on March 12, 2024, in room 2.01
of the Montreal Courthouse.
[21]

[
55
]

On March 11, 2024, the Defendant was once again
informed by email from the trial Judge that the trial would take place on the
following day in room 15.05 of the Montreal Courthouse.
[22]

[
56
]

In any event, the Defendant admits that she knew
the trial would take place on March 12.

[
57
]

Despite being informed of the date of the trial
on numerous occasions, and despite being aware of the trial date, the Defendant
did not attend the trial.

[
58
]

The minutes of the March 12 hearing indicate:

Puisque Mme T... a été dûment
signifiée et devrait être au courant de l’audience de ce jour, le Tribunal note
son absence et
ORDONNE
que l’audience procède par défaut.

[
59
]

The Judgment of Divorce was issued on the
following day, March 13, 2024.

[
60
]

There is no basis in fact and in law to revoke
the Judgment of Divorce for the reason that she was prevented from defending
the Divorce Application on the merits owing to fraud or surprise or any other
cause considered sufficient.

[
61
]

Moreover, her physical or mental health cannot
constitute a valid reason justifying her failure to attend the trial. While she
has filed in support of her Application for Revocation excerpts from her
medical file attesting to physical ailments which she suffered, nothing in the
documentary evidence establishes that she had a valid medical reason which
explains her absence on the trial date.
[23]

[
62
]

Moreover, she did not testify during the
September 18 hearing with respect to a physical or mental ailment preventing
her from attending the trial, nor did she adduce an expert report proving that
she could not attend owing to medical reasons.

[
63
]

For all these reasons, and subject to the
religious belief argument which is addressed below, the only reason the
Defendant did not attend the trial is because of her negligence and
carelessness.

2.3

Does Letting the Judgment of Divorce Stand Bring the Administration of
Justice into Disrepute owing to the Defendant’s Religious Beliefs Prohibiting Divorce?

[
64
]

In her Application, the Defendant argues that
the Judgment of Divorce should be revoked because her religious beliefs
precluded her from attending the trial:

32. I was unable to attend the
scheduled court date due to deeply held religious beliefs that prohibit
divorce.

33. As devoted chosen one by God and
Jesus by heart divorce is contrary to the fundamental tenets of my faith.

(sic)

[
65
]

In her May 3 judgment, Justice Dubé writes:

[32]

In her application in
revocation
, the
Defendant explicitly invokes her religious beliefs, which prohibit divorce, as the
cause of her inability to defend herself. However, she does not allege how they
prevented her from asserting her patrimonial rights. Furthermore, the grounds
of defence raised in her application in
revocation
relate
to these rights, and not to the granting of the divorce itself.
Therefore,
prima facie
, the reason explicitly invoked does not
explain the default.

[
66
]

The Defendant testified at the September 18
hearing, albeit for a very brief period. Her testimony was vague and lacked any
detail whatsoever with respect to her religious beliefs, other than to reassert
that she could not attend the trial because it was in her own words, “difficult”
to do so because of her religious beliefs. She added that the Judgment of
Divorce made no sense and was unfair, although she could not explain how it was
unfair.

[
67
]

She did add in cross-examination that the
religious beliefs that she relies upon in support of her Application for
Revocation is a belief that existed at the time the Application for Divorce was
filed in July 2022 and is a belief she still holds to this day.

[
68
]

She also stated that she wishes to reconcile
with the Plaintiff. Yet, she also recognizes that it is within his right to
obtain a divorce.

[
69
]

Marriage and divorce fall under the exclusive
jurisdiction of the Parliament of Canada, while the provinces have jurisdiction
over the solemnization of marriage.

[
70
]

The Parliament of Canada adopted the
Divorce
Act
in 1968 and since then, all Canadians have the right to apply for and
obtain a judgment of divorce in regard to a civil marriage.

[
71
]

In
Bruker
v
. Marcovitz
, the
Supreme Court of Canada writes
[24]
:

[92]

The public interest in protecting equality rights, the
dignity of Jewish women in their independent ability to divorce and remarry, as
well as the public benefit in enforcing valid and binding contractual
obligations, are among the interests and values that outweigh Mr. Marcovitz’s
claim that enforcing Paragraph 12 of the Consent would interfere with his
religious freedom.

[
72
]

In the Court’s view,
Bruker
precludes the
Defendant from raising her religious belief as a reason to prevent the
Plaintiff from asserting his right to obtain a divorce. Moreover,
Bruker

establishes that letting the Judgment of Divorce stand notwithstanding the
Defendant’s religious beliefs would not tend to bring the administration of
justice into disrepute.

[
73
]

In
Droit de la
famille — 22187
, the Court
writes
[25]
:

[70]        Monsieur’s refusal to
agree to religious divorce, in the context described above, also amounts to an
unlawful interference with Madam’s rights to freedom, to dignity, to equality,
and not to be harassed on the basis of her gender under the Québec Charter. His
conduct harms both Madam personally and the public’s interest in protecting
fundamental values such as equality rights and autonomous choice in marriage
and divorce.

[Citations omitted]

[
74
]

The Court held in this case that according to
Québec case law, a spouse under a civil marriage has a fundamental right to
obtain a judgment of divorce and his former spouse’s unjustifiable refusal to
agree to religious divorce, can constitute a civil fault as per the laws of
this province and triggers his civil liability. In unjustifiably refusing to
agree to the religious divorce, the husband unlawfully and intentionally limited
his wife’s rights and freedoms.
[26]

[
75
]

These precedents stand for the proposition that
the Plaintiff had a fundamental right, both under the
Canadian
Charter of
Rights and Freedoms
and the Québec
Charter
to obtain a judgment of
divorce notwithstanding the Defendant’s religious beliefs.

[
76
]

Hence, not attending the trial of the divorce
action because of her “deeply held religious beliefs that prohibit divorce” was
the Defendant’s personal choice, but it cannot constitute a reason that letting
the Judgment of Divorce stand would tend to bring the administration of justice
into disrepute.

[
77
]

Moreover, the Defendant’s argument is also
inconsistent with the underlying rationale for
section 21.1
of the
Divorce
Act
.

[
78
]

This provision of the
Divorce Act
was
adopted to prevent one of the spouses, in civil divorce proceedings, from using
his or her refusal to grant a religious divorce as a bargaining tool to obtain
concessions from the other spouse in his or her civil divorce application. One
can well imagine a situation where a wife could be forced to make concessions
in civil divorce proceedings on issues such as parenting time or alimony, in
order to obtain her ex-spouse's cooperation in obtaining a religious divorce
[27]
.

[
79
]

If a spouse’s refusal to consent to a religious
divorce cannot prevent the other spouse from obtaining a divorce under the
Divorce
Act
, than a
fortiori
a religious belief that divorce is prohibited
under one’s religion cannot be a ground to justify one’s failure to attend a
divorce proceeding and then seeking the revocation of the judgment of divorce.

[
80
]

In short, the religious beliefs of the Defendant
cannot stand in the way of the Plaintiff’s right to obtain a judgment of
divorce under the
Divorce Act
. With this principle in mind, not attending
the divorce trial because of the Defendant’s religious beliefs is not a valid reason
for revocating the Judgment of Divorce.

[
81
]

Moreover, because of the Defendant’s past
conduct in this case, the Court gives little probative value to her assertion
that her religious belief prevented her from attending the trial. Raising her
religious beliefs is a pretext to avoid the consequences of the Judgment of
Divorce.

[
82
]

The Application to divorce was served on the
Defendant in July 2022.

[
83
]

On July 25, she filed an answer to the
proceeding through legal counsel indicating that she intended to contest the
application for divorce and establish a case protocol; she also proposed
mediation and a settlement conference.

[
84
]

On October 26, 2022, her lawyer filed with the
Plaintiff’s lawyer a case protocol. Nowhere in the document did she raise any
objection to the divorce application on religious grounds. To the contrary, she
attorned to the subject matter jurisdiction of the Court and indicated she
intended to file an application for provisional measures and a cross-demand.

[
85
]

On April 20, 2023, the Defendant filed a
cross-demand in which she did not raise or assert any objection, based on
religious beliefs or otherwise, to the divorce application.

[
86
]

Quite the contrary, she herself asked the Court
to grant a divorce between the parties and asserted rights with respect to
accessory measures, including partition of the family patrimony, and partition
of the partnership of acquests. Moreover, she also sought
relief at the provisional and safeguard stage.

[
87
]

The Court concludes that the Defendant lacks
credibility when she raises her religious belief as the reason why she did not
attend the trial.

[
88
]

Moreover, her legal syllogism is contradictory
and lacks logic.  If she could not attend the divorce trial in March 2024
because of her religious beliefs, and since she holds these same beliefs today,
then what purpose is there in revoking the Judgment of Divorce? Revocation
implies that “the parties are restored to their former state » (art. 348
C.C.P.
),
and that a new trial will be scheduled.

[
89
]

But since she holds the same religious beliefs, then
she won’t be able to attend the second trial and it will proceed by default
anew. This is tantamount to a Catch 22 situation.

[
90
]

The interests of justice are not served by
recognising the Defendant’s religious beliefs as a reason to revoke the Divorce
Judgment.

[
91
]

Finally, the Defendant’s claim that the Judgment
of Divorce is unfair is without merit.

[
92
]

Firstly, she was unable to explain the basis of
this argument.

[
93
]

Secondly, the Judgment of Divorce is consistent
with the public order rules contained in the
Divorce Act
and the
Civil
Code of Québec

governing the dissolution of the family patrimony and the
matrimonial regime.

[
94
]

In his Application for Divorce, the Plaintiff
asks for the partition of the family patrimony and the parties’ matrimonial
regime (partnership of acquests) in a manner consistent with the rules set
forth in the
Civil Code of Québec
.

[
95
]

Plaintiff abided with his obligation to provide
a full and frank disclosure of his assets. The Defendant did not.

[
96
]

The trial judge was presented detailed evidence
of the Plaintiff’s statement of family patrimony and of partnership of acquests
[28]
with all the relevant
supporting evidence.
[29]

[
97
]

The trial judge partitioned the family patrimony
and the matrimonial regime into equal shares.

[
98
]

It was the Defendant’s burden to prove that the
Judgment of Divorce is not consistent with the public order rules set forth in
the
Civil Code of Québec
. She has not discharged this burden.

[
99
]

Finally, it is not necessary to assess the
seriousness of the Defendant’s grounds of defense since the rule expressed by
the Court of Appeal in
Groupe JSV
[30]

only applies when the application for revocation relies solely on article 346
C.C.P.

[
100
]

In the case at the bar, the Defendant’s
Application for Revocation truly rests on article 345
C.C.P.
Moreover,
the Defendant has already filed a defense and cross-demand to the Plaintiff’s
Application to Institute Proceedings in Divorce. Finally, if it is necessary to
evaluate the seriousness of the grounds of defense alleged in her Application
for Revocation, the Court considers that they are weak and are not serious.

[
101
]

The revocation of a judgment is an exception to
the well established and important principle pertaining to the finality and
stability of civil judgments.

[
102
]

In the instant case, the reasons raised by the
Defendant to obtain the revocation of the Judgment of Divorce are unfounded.

[
103
]

The Defendant is using her Application for Revocation
as a tactic to relitigate a matter that has already been decided by the Court
and for which she was duly notified of the trial date.

[
104
]

The Application to Revoke the Judgment of Divorce
will be dismissed. None of the conditions set forth in articles 345 or 346 of
the
Code of Civil Procedure
for the
revocation
of
judgment
have been
proved.

[
105
]

The Petitioner’s allegations are unsubstantiated
and not supported by the evidence.

[
106
]

She has not convinced the Court that the
principle of the stability of judgments should be set aside, namely because she
was prevented from attending the trial owing to fraud, surprise or any other
cause considered sufficient.

[
107
]

Moreover, she has not convinced the Court that letting
the Judgment of Divorce stand would tend to bring the administration of justice
into disrepute. Despite her religious beliefs, the very basis of the Judgment
of Divorce is not seriously and irreparably flawed.

FOR THESE
REASONS, THE COURT:

[
108
]

DISMISSES
the
Defendant’s Application for Revocation of the March 13, 2024 judgment of
divorce;

[
109
]
